_channel.name: Map Paradox
_channel.footer:
Map data: Natural Earth (public domain). Narration: AI voice (Kokoro). Music: YouTube Audio Library.
#maps #geography #shorts

w001.title: London is further north than Calgary 🤯 #maps
w001.hook: Europe is way further north than you think.
w001.desc:
London (51.5°N) sits further north than Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto and Montreal. Paris is further north than Seattle, Rome higher than New York.
Why is Europe so mild? The Gulf Stream helps, but research (Seager et al., 2002) shows the bigger factor is westerly winds blowing over a warm ocean.

Sources: Natural Earth coordinates; Seager R. et al. (2002), Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society.

w002.title: Africa is 14x bigger than Greenland 🌍 #maps
w002.hook: This map has lied to you your whole life.
w002.desc:
On the Mercator map Greenland looks as big as Africa. In reality Africa (30.4M km²) is about 14 times larger than Greenland (2.2M km²). The US, China and India together still fit inside Africa.

Sources: CIA World Factbook (areas); Mercator projection, Gerardus Mercator, 1569.
w002.comment: Which country do you think is the most distorted on maps?

w003.title: 2 out of 3 Canadians live in this tiny strip 🇨🇦 #maps
w003.hook: Canada is the second biggest country on Earth, but almost nobody lives in it.
w003.desc:
About two thirds of Canadians live within 100 km of the US border. Canada has ~41.5 million people, close to California's ~39.4 million.

Sources: Statistics Canada (2017 border-distance analysis; 2025 population estimate); US Census Bureau (2024 estimate).
w003.comment: Would you live in northern Canada? 🥶

w004.title: Russia is bigger than Pluto 🪐 #maps
w004.hook: Russia is bigger than the entire surface of Pluto.
w004.desc:
Russia covers 17.1M km²; Pluto's whole surface is about 16.7M km². Russia spans 11 time zones: 8 AM in Kaliningrad is 6 PM in Kamchatka. Around three quarters of Russians live west of the Urals.

Sources: CIA World Factbook; NASA (Pluto); IANA time zone database.
w004.comment: What's the biggest country you've visited?

w005.title: 20% of the world's oil goes through this gap ⛽ #maps
w005.hook: One fifth of all the oil the world uses passes through this tiny gap.
w005.desc:
About 20 million barrels per day, roughly 20% of global petroleum consumption, pass through the Strait of Hormuz (2024). At its narrowest it is about 33 km (21 miles) wide, with two-mile shipping lanes each way. Bypass pipelines can carry only a small share.

Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), World Oil Transit Chokepoints / Hormuz analysis 2024–2025.
w005.comment: Which chokepoint should we map next?

w006.title: France's longest border is with… Brazil 🇫🇷🇧🇷 #maps
w006.hook: France's longest land border isn't in Europe.
w006.desc:
French Guiana is a full part of France (and the EU), so France shares a 649 km border with Brazil, just ahead of Spain (646 km), per the CIA World Factbook. With its overseas territories France has 12 time zones, the most of any country.

Sources: CIA World Factbook (border lengths); French government (time zones).
w006.comment: Did you know French Guiana uses the euro? 💶

w007.title: Chile on top of Europe is insane 🇨🇱 #maps
w007.hook: Chile is the strangest shaped country on Earth.
w007.desc:
Chile is about 4,300 km long but averages only around 180 km wide. Moved onto Europe at true size, it would stretch from Arctic Norway almost to North Africa. From the Atacama, one of the driest deserts on Earth, to southern glaciers.

Sources: CIA World Factbook; Encyclopaedia Britannica.
w007.comment: Which country should we drop on Europe next?

w008.title: Indonesia is wider than the USA 🇮🇩 #maps
w008.hook: Indonesia is wider than the United States.
w008.desc:
Indonesia spans more than 5,000 km west to east, wider than the contiguous United States. It has 17,000+ islands and about 280 million people, the world's 4th largest population.

Sources: Indonesian Geospatial Information Agency (BIG); CIA World Factbook.

w009.title: 95% of Egypt lives on this thin line 🇪🇬 #maps
w009.desc:
About 95% of Egyptians live within 20 km of the Nile and its delta; the rest of the country is Sahara. The Nile flows north for more than 6,000 km and Egypt is the last country it reaches.

Sources: CIA World Factbook (population distribution); CAPMAS (population, 2024).
w009.comment: Would you live in the desert or by the river? 🏜️

w010.title: This 82 km ditch saves ships 12,600 km 🚢 #maps
w010.desc:
The Panama Canal cuts 12,668 km (7,872 mi) off a New York–San Francisco voyage. Locks lift ships 26 m to Gatún Lake; each transit uses ~200 million liters of fresh water, which is why the 2023 drought forced cuts. Roughly 5% of world sea trade passes through.

Sources: Panama Canal Authority; Encyclopaedia Britannica.
w010.comment: Suez or Panama, which is more important? 🤔

w011.title: The emptiest country on Earth 🇲🇳 #maps
w011.desc:
Mongolia (1.56M km²) is bigger than France, Germany, Italy and the UK combined, yet has only ~3.5 million people, about 2 per km². Almost half live in Ulaanbaatar, the world's coldest capital.

Sources: National Statistics Office of Mongolia; CIA World Factbook.
w011.comment: Could you handle a winter in Ulaanbaatar? 🥶

w012.title: Australia vs USA at true size 🇦🇺 #maps
w012.desc:
Australia (7.7M km²) is almost as big as the contiguous United States (8.1M km²), but has ~27 million people vs ~340 million. About 85% of Australians live within 50 km of the coast.

Sources: Australian Bureau of Statistics; Geoscience Australia; US Census Bureau.
w012.comment: Which Aussie city would you pick? 🦘

w013.title: The busiest oil route on Earth is 2.8 km wide ⛽ #maps
w013.desc:
About 23.7 million barrels of oil a day passed through the Strait of Malacca in 2023, more than Hormuz, mostly bound for China, Japan and South Korea. Near Singapore the Phillips Channel narrows to about 2.8 km (1.7 mi).

Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), World Oil Transit Chokepoints.
w013.comment: Malacca or Hormuz, which matters more?

w014.title: This lake holds more water than all 5 Great Lakes 💧 #maps
w014.desc:
Lake Baikal holds ~23,600 km³ of water, more than all five Great Lakes combined (~22,700 km³), about 20% of Earth's unfrozen surface fresh water. It is the deepest (1,642 m) and oldest (~25 million years) lake in the world.

Sources: UNESCO World Heritage; USGS; US EPA (Great Lakes).

w015.title: The US bought Alaska for 2 cents an acre 🇺🇸 #maps
w015.desc:
In 1867 the US bought Alaska from Russia for $7.2 million, about 2 cents per acre. Alaska (1.72M km²) is bigger than Texas, California and Montana combined. Big and Little Diomede islands are less than 4 km apart.

Sources: US National Archives (Treaty with Russia, 1867); US Census Bureau.
w015.comment: Best deal or worst deal in history?

w016.title: Brazil is bigger than the USA 🇧🇷 #maps
w016.desc:
Brazil (8.5M km²) is bigger than the 48 contiguous US states (8.1M km²). It borders 10 countries — every South American country except Chile and Ecuador — and holds about 60% of the Amazon rainforest.

Sources: CIA World Factbook; IBGE.

w017.title: One ship blocked $9.6 billion a day 🚢 #maps
w017.desc:
In March 2021 the Ever Given blocked the Suez Canal for six days, holding up an estimated $9.6 billion of trade per day (Lloyd's List). The 193 km canal carries about 12% of world trade; going around Africa adds roughly 10 days.

Sources: Suez Canal Authority; Lloyd's List (2021).
w017.comment: Do you remember the Ever Given memes? 😅

w018.title: A country trapped inside another country 🇱🇸 #maps
w018.desc:
Lesotho is completely surrounded by South Africa, one of only three fully enclaved countries (with San Marino and Vatican City). Its lowest point is about 1,400 m, the highest 'lowest point' of any country, and it sells water to South Africa through the Lesotho Highlands Water Project.

Sources: CIA World Factbook; Government of Lesotho.
w018.comment: Did you know it snows in Africa? ❄️

w019.title: The world's biggest lake is called a sea 🌊 #maps
w019.desc:
The Caspian Sea (~371,000 km²) has no outlet to the ocean and is bigger than Germany. Five countries share it, and because of its oil and gas, 'sea or lake' matters — the 2018 convention gave it a special status that is neither.

Sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica; Convention on the Legal Status of the Caspian Sea (2018).

w020.title: Spain has a border with Africa 🇪🇸🇲🇦 #maps
w020.desc:
Ceuta and Melilla are Spanish cities on the African coast, part of Spain and the EU, and the EU's only land borders in mainland Africa. Europe and Africa are about 14 km apart at the Strait of Gibraltar, and Gibraltar itself is British.

Sources: CIA World Factbook; Encyclopaedia Britannica.
w020.comment: Have you crossed the Strait of Gibraltar? ⛴️

w021.title: Japan is bigger than Germany 🇯🇵 #maps
w021.desc:
Japan (~378,000 km²) is bigger than Germany (~357,600 km²), Italy or the UK. Dropped on Europe at true size it stretches about 3,000 km. About three quarters of Japan is mountainous, so most people live on the flat coasts.

Sources: CIA World Factbook; Statistics Bureau of Japan.
w021.comment: Which country should we compare next?
